ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, \(AB\) is the diameter of the circle \(\odot O\), and \(CD\) is a chord. If \(\angle BCD=34^\circ\), then what is the measure of \(\angle ABD\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that AB is the diameter of circle O, \\
thus, $\angle ADB=90^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle DAB + \angle ABD = 90^\circ$, \\
since $\angle DAB = \angle BCD = 34^\circ$, \\
thus, $\angle ABD = 90^\circ - 34^\circ = \boxed{56^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A and B are opposite endpoints of the circle’s diameter, D lies on the upper semicircle between A and B, and C lies on the lower-right arc; ∠BCD intercepts the minor arc BD, and ∠ABD intercepts arc AD.
